# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 18 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** PSO 18 | **Agents:** EMET / LOGOS / PNEUMA / SOPHIA

---

**Total disagreements:** 6

**1. 18:1**
EMET: 'thy goodness [is] over Israel with a rich gift.' LOGOS: 'your kindness covers Israel as a rich gift.' PNEUMA: 'your goodness covers Israel like a lavish gift.' All render the same image; PNEUMA adds 'lavish.'

**2. 18:4**
EMET: 'as [upon] a firstborn son, the only-born.' LOGOS: 'as upon a firstborn, an only son.' PNEUMA: 'as on a firstborn, an only child.' The double designation (firstborn + only) is important — echoes Isaac typology.

**3. 18:5-9**
These verses closely parallel Ps 17:21-46 conclusion and Ps 5:4-9. This is a deliberate closing refrain of the collection. All agents note the structural parallel.

**4. 18:7**
All four agents agree: 'in the spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength.' This triple gift of the spirit echoes Isa 11:2 (the messianic spirit). The anointed one of vv.5-7 is consistent with Ps 17's messianic king.

**5. 18:11-14**
The closing meditation on the faithful stars/lights maintaining their God-ordained courses serves as a cosmic analogy: just as the heavenly lights do not deviate from God's command, so the messianic king will not deviate from righteousness. PNEUMA: most expansive in v.11, 'to mark off the seasons year after year.'

**6. 18:14**
EMET: 'by the command of his servants.' LOGOS/SOPHIA: 'by the word of his servants.' PNEUMA: 'through the word of his servants.' 'Servants' = prophets. The lights obey God through prophetic command — an unusual cosmology.
